Title: API Feature Request Programmatic Access Feature Flag
Details:
API Feature Request: Programmatic Access to Feature Flag / Experiment Activity Log
User Story:
As an API user, I want to retrieve the full historical activity log for each feature flag and experiment, including events like 'paused', 'resumed', 'archived', and changes to traffic allocation.
Business Value & Use Case:
The excellent "Activity Log" feature is currently available in the Kameleoon UI, but this data is not exposed through the public API. Programmatic access to this log would unlock several key capabilities for us:
Automated Auditing & Compliance: For compliance and incident review, we need to maintain a programmatic record of when experiments are activated or deactivated in our production environment.
Real-time Alerting: We want to build automations that trigger alerts in our internal systems (like Slack or PagerDuty) whenever the state of a critical feature flag is changed.
Performance Correlation: Access to these event timestamps would allow us to automatically correlate experiment pause/resume events with our internal performance metrics (e.g., site latency, error rates) to quickly understand the impact of any changes.
Currently, the API only provides the dateModified timestamp, which doesn't specify what changed. This requires us to perform manual checks in the UI, which is not scalable for our monitoring and auditing needs.
Suggested Solution:
A potential solution could be a new endpoint, for example: GET /feature-flags/{featureKey}/activity-log.
This endpoint could return a list of event objects, each containing details like the timestamp, the user who made the change, the action performed (e.g., 'paused_rollout_rule'), and any relevant details.
Exposing this data via the API would significantly enhance our ability to integrate Kameleoon into our automated DevOps and compliance workflows.

Title: Anonymizing url parameter
Details:
Anonymizing url parameter
=========================
Sometimes "zip code" or "order number" or other none critical PII are available as page url parameter (e.g. ?orderNo=123456&zip=abcd12&utm_category=Shirt&utm_campaign=1234...) - even though best practice would be not using it. However, not all tools already work that way so they are required/used... In those cases we have to deactivate the entire "main JS" to protect the customer data if PII is part of page url.
This feature would allow url parameters to be anonymized before the page url is collected and stored to the back-end by the "main JS".
It needs to be defined before the page url is stored in the back-end and could have an user-defined object list of url parameter like ['param1','param2'] which is used to iterate through all existing url parameter. If it is a match, then the value of the matched parameter is hashed or set to a default like "ANONYMIZED".

Title: Close to Fastly
Details:
Close to Fastly. Already integrated by severals competitors: Paired with tools like Statsig, HappyKit, Split, and other experimentation partners, Edge Config can drastically improve performance and load experience. By integrating these tools with Edge Config, their data gets pushed to the edge when it's changed. When a user visits your site, no extra network requests are needed to retrieve the config data. What's more, since the data is globally distributed, latency for the initial read is reduced. Compute before the cache
When compute happens instantly, routing decisions can be made before the cache. Making A/B testing and feature flagging possible without added third-party scripts or client-side JavaScript. https://vercel.com/blog/edge-config-public-beta

Title: Concerning use Predictive Targeting module
Details:
Concerning the use of the IA Predictive Targeting module
In my various discussions with customers on this subject, I've noticed that using the word “Trigger” when configuring the IA Predictive goal doesn't necessarily make sense. In fact, the addition doesn't “trigger” anything, as an action in itself. It's a way of recording data based on one or more key moments in the user journey.
This becomes even more complex with the new segment builder, because when an experience is created, this is what happens.
In targeting, we select a Predictive AI condition.
We select the goal from which we want to load user heat scores + a trigger from the list of associated key moments (to refine the curve we want to use). This trigger doesn't trigger anything in the experiment configuration, it's only linked to the AI goal.
BUT you'll also need to add segment OR trigger elements to the experience targeting to indicate when/where/to whom this experience should be displayed. The trigger can be the same as that used for the AI goal, or completely different.
In short, I simply note that the use of "trigger" terminology in the experience is hardly palpable in the context of a campaign that uses an AI goal. Perhaps the use of Key Moments, as historically could help make this clearer.

Title: Consider adding DMA Designated Market Area something
Details:
Please consider adding DMA (Designated Market Area), or something similar, to items available to pick for IP Geolocation when creating a segment.  For example, we have a strong need to be able to target visitors in the Los Angeles metro area.  If we choose "Los Angeles" as the setting, it only matches visitors who have exactly "Los Angeles" come back as their city value when the lookup is performed.  This ends up actually being a rather small area, as there are a lot of other "cities" contained within not only the city of Los Angeles itself, but also the immediate surrounding area.  For example, the city value may come back as "West Hollywood" when the lookup is performed, which most people would consider to be definitely within Los Angeles. Yet the segment does not match if it is defined as "United States, California, Los Angeles".  Using the state of California, the next largest available option, is too large.
The current workaround is to use a bunch of zipcodes in the Experiment Code and calculate entry qualification there (using the values in Kameleoon.API.CurrentVisit.geolocation), but it would be much simpler, and a more obvious setup to those who are reviewing the experiment, to be able to do it in a segment.

Title: Currently bulk editing users only allows deactivating
Details:
Currently, bulk editing of users only allows deactivating or deleting accounts. It would be highly valuable to also have the ability to bulk edit project permissions and account permissions.
Why it matters:
	•	Managing larger organizations with many users is time-consuming when permissions need to be updated one by one.
	•	With account permissions specifically, it would be very helpful to bulk edit solutions (e.g., enable/disable Web Experimentation or Feature Experimentation) for multiple users at once.
	•	This would reduce admin overhead, improve consistency, and make it easier to onboard or adjust access for entire teams.
Proposed functionality:
	•	Extend bulk edit options beyond deactivate/delete.
	•	Allow selection of multiple users to update:
	•	Project permissions (product/marketing/technical/admin)
	•	Account permissions, including toggling solutions (Web Experimentation, Feature Experimentation).
This would save significant time for admins, reduces risk of inconsistent permission setups, and improves scalability for organizations managing dozens or hundreds of users.

Title: Customized time interval MAB option
Details:
Customized time interval for the MAB option:
Pain Point:
- there is a global time interval of 8h
- As a client with low traffic, I don't always achieve the 100 visits and 20 conversions in the winning variant (perhaps I would have needed 11 hours). In such cases, no adjustment happens. => my opportunity costs increase
- As a high-traffic client, I reach the 100 visits and 20 conversions in the winning variant much faster than in 8 hours (e.g. in 1 hour). In such cases, the adjustment still only happens every 8 hours. => my opportunity costs increase
- As a client with a content business model, I have a lot of traffic, no time for long test periods (because the articles quickly lose their relevance) and want to test teasers or headlines with a primary click target. The 100 visits and 20 conversions in the winning variant are achieved much faster than in 8 hours (e.g. in 0.1 hours). In such cases, the adjustment still only happens every 8 hours. => my opportunity costs increase
Solution:
- Individual client setting: I can set a time interval for my account that applies to all projects and experiments.
- Project individual setting: I can set a time interval for my projects that applies to all experiments in the respective project. (see Perso control group)
- Experiment individual setting: I can set a time interval for my experiments that only applies to the individual experiment. (see MBA option itself)

Tldr: only take into account in the results time periods when the experiment was live

Title: Feature Request Consolidated Reporting Related Experiments
Details:
Feature Request: Consolidated Reporting for Related Experiments
Feature Title: Ability to Group and View Aggregated Results for Multiple, Related Experiments
Problem Description:
When conducting A/B tests or personalization campaigns across different languages, regions, or closely related segments, it is often necessary or beneficial to set up separate experiments for each. For example, a global brand might run identical or similar tests on their German (DE) and French (FR) websites, resulting in "Test A (DE)" and "Test A (FR)" as distinct experiments in Kameleoon.
Currently, Kameleoon's reporting interface only allows users to view the results for one experiment at a time. To understand the overall performance across all related tests (e.g., the combined impact of "Test A" across both DE and FR), users are forced to analyise the data outside of Kameleoon (e.g. Google Analytics)
This process is time-consuming, and hinders the ability to quickly grasp the cumulative impact of a strategic initiative within Kameleoon itself. It also fragments the analysis workflow and reduces the perceived value of Kameleoon as a primary analytics source.
Possible Solution:
We request a feature that allows users to group related experiments and view their aggregated results within a single, consolidated report in Kameleoon.
Tags: new idea, nice to have, Ex owner: Calixthe Mattei, Q2 2025, App System, Processed

Title: Feature Request Page-Specific CSS Selectors Graphic Editor
Details:
Feature Request: Page-Specific CSS Selectors in Graphic Editor
Allow users to specify the scope of CSS selectors in the graphic editor to apply modifications only to selected pages, avoiding unintended changes across multiple pages with common selectors.
Currently, when using the graphic editor, modifications are applied based on CSS selectors. If a selector is present on multiple pages, the changes affect all instances across the campaign. This becomes an issue when a user wants to apply different modifications to specific pages but cannot do so because the selector is not unique to a single page.
For example, on e-commerce sites, product description sections often share the same class (e.g., .ProductDescription). If a user modifies this class in the visual editor, the change is applied globally across all product pages, rather than being limited to a specific set of URLs or product types. This limitation forces users to write custom code to scope their modifications, which is not ideal for those unfamiliar with coding.
For now, it seems that the system applies runWhenElementPresent behind the scenes when a CSS selector is chosen in the visual editor. It would be great to have the option to add an includes condition for the page URL, either with a regex pattern or a flat URL match. This would allow non-technical users to easily restrict their modifications to specific pages without having to write custom JavaScript conditions manually.

Details:
Integrate the Kameleoon Visitor Code with the GA4 experience_impression event
This will be helpful for an easier/efficient capture of the Visitor Code for GA4. It doesn't make sense for it to have its own GA4 event because it would be essentially be firing at the same time as page views and that's a waste of event hits when you can integrate it with the existing pageview event.

Traffic allocation:
Many clients forget about our recommendation to don't change the traffic allocation from the moment the experiment is live and others want to do it anyway.
The most natural way to do it is from the code editor.
The idea is to change the logic of the reallocation from the code editor:
1. by default visitors stay bucketed in the same variation before and after reallocation;
2. the client can use a checkbox (next to each variation and original) if they desire to allow the change of a visitor's variation (with this information in a tooltip)

Code versioning (Code editor and GS):
Today, if a change is made, the previous version of code is lost.
It would be very practical to offer the clients the possibility of saving the code and then getting it back from the history created. So they won't worry about losing a version or saving it elsewhere before making a change.
This is an AB tasty feature.

---

Code export:
Some clients want to export an experiment code to save it elsewhere, before stopping an experiment or any other reason.
If the experiment has 2 variations for example, they will need to copy paste up to 6 scripts manually to save them.
It would be nice to be able to export the code, organised by variation, with a single button.
This is an AB Tasty feature

Details:
Our busniess operates in a context with some really massive customers, causeing many non-binary metrics to be unrealiable and frequent spikes when looking at graphs

---

---

Really interesting for us to get the highest quality and insights possible!

it's very needed for many of our metrics such as add to cart and save to list when slicing on all conversions level

---

Otherwise some experiments will be destroyed

---

The significant variation in our customers' sizes necessitates outlier handling for more aspects than just revenue.

---

The new feature enhances outlier detection by analyzing unusual patterns in various metrics, such as extreme user behaviors. This automatic filtering of atypical data ensures more reliable and actionable test insights.

---

We’d like to highlight an urgent need for Metric-based Outlier Filtering in Kameleoon.
Currently, the Winsorization approach handles revenue data, but we increasingly see outlier behavior in other metrics — particularly users with unusually high frequencies of “add to cart” or purchase events. These extreme patterns distort test results and reduce trust in the statistical validity of our A/B insights.
If this isn’t addressed within Kameleoon, we’ll be forced to build a custom pre-filtering process to remove such users before running tests — which would compromise statistical integrity and duplicate functionality that ideally belongs in the platform.
A more comprehensive outlier filtering mechanism, considering behavioral metrics as well, would greatly improve the reliability and confidence in our experimentation results.
Best regards,
Peter

The importance of the "New filter: Do not show products with at least one category matching those of the items in the cart" feature lies in its ability to refine and tailor product recommendations, ultimately improving the user experience and driving sales on the e-commerce website's recommendations block.
Diversified Product Suggestions: By excluding products with categories that match those of items already in the cart, this feature ensures that users are presented with a diverse range of options. Prevention of Redundancy: Redundant recommendations can be off-putting to users and may lead to a perception of limited selection or lack of variety. By filtering out products with overlapping categories, the feature helps avoid redundancy in recommendations, maintaining user interest and engagement with the recommendations block.
Encouragement of Product Discovery: Excluding products that fall within the same categories as items in the cart promotes product discovery and exploration. Users are more likely to encounter new and different products that they may be interested in, expanding their shopping experience and potentially increasing their order size as they discover additional items of interest.
Optimized User Experience: Providing users with a curated selection of product recommendations that complement their existing cart items improves the overall user experience. By presenting relevant yet distinct options, the feature streamlines the shopping process and ensures that users encounter products that genuinely pique their interest, leading to greater satisfaction with the website's recommendations block.
Increased Conversion Rates: When users are presented with a varied selection of products that align with their interests but do not duplicate items already in their cart, they are more likely to make additional purchases. This can lead to increased conversion rates as users are enticed to explore and add more items to their cart, ultimately driving revenue for the e-commerce website.
In summary, the "New filter: Do not show products with at least one category matching those of the items in the cart" feature is crucial for optimizing the recommendations block on an e-commerce website. By promoting diversified product suggestions, preventing redundancy, encouraging product discovery, optimizing the user experience, and increasing conversion rates, this feature contributes significantly to the success of the recommendations block and the overall performance of the e-commerce platform.

Title: Raw Data export 2.0
Details:
Pain Points:   Enterprise: A medium/large customer quickly reaches 100k as a data volume in an experiment. Free export is no longer possible for such experiments. Theoretically it could be exported over several months in smaller periods. But this is impractical and inefficient. Such a customer therefore never has the opportunity to make even one complete export. They therefore never get to know the feature and cannot discover any benefits from it. Which is to Kameleoon's disadvantage. In a direct customer comparison this is unfair because a small customer runs 1-3 raw data exports per month (for free), which may also correspond to their output. So a small customer has his raw data for almost every experiment, while larger customers cannot use it without additional costs.    Debugging/CSM: customers build goals, CDs and co. themselves. In addition to qualitative quality management, quantitative quality management is often also useful. This can easily be done via a raw data export. The raw data therefore helps with quality management without having any "direct business added value". Above all if customers don't find mistakes they cannot even go into debugging independently. Because the access to the raw data export is missing/limited. At such times they end up with the CSM. The CSM is now faced with the dilemma of offering the upsell or helping out with a billable export themselves.   Aggregated exports: Customers don't always understand the difference between aggregated and raw data. Nor about the technical efforts & costs behind it. Why one is behind a paywall and the other isn't leads to even more disagreement.   Data authority: Customers find it unfair that their data is deliberately kept behind a pay wall   Transparency: the customer has no transparency about his already exported data points. It could be 0 or 99,999 - they're only informed via a pop-up that they will not receive their export. He doesn't know whether he could possibly receive the export with a small period adjustment. Also the CSM as the first point of contact doesn't know.   All-teams approach: it isn't uncommon for exports to be made sporadically. For customers with several modules, several teams are usually involved, which export independently of each other. It sometimes happens that the FE team “steals” the export budget from the WebEx team without them knowing or being able to oversee it.   User role: There is currently no option to prohibit the export of raw data for some roles. Anyone from marketing to Super Admin can request a raw data export and thus use the “budget”.   Technical customers: the increasing number of feature experimentation customers and due to the all-teams approach leads to more operational contacts with very good technical understanding. For them it's quite obvious that the raw data query has low costs for us and that the pricing therefore contains a very large margin. Answer from a client after he received the pricing: Are your costs for the queries that high? The data is stored in a Cassandra DB regardless of our query limit, right? I would expect such a simple raw data export without complex calculations to cost a maximum of 1€ per query.   Sales: Operational Kameleoon users predominantly don't like sales processes and have no direct budget responsibility. It always creates a bad mood when they receive the limit popup in kameleoon and/or the feedback from CSMs with the 100k limit. Usually the operational processes then come to a standstill. In most cases short-term compromises are then made (with service) and the sales process is started in parallel. This often starts with low customer satisfaction.    Pricing Solutions:   annual budget: The budget is no longer monthly, but annual. This means that each customer could export 1.2 million data points per year until they reach the threshold. As a first upsell, the threshold would be up to 12 million data points per year. Unlimited is retained anyway. (Disadvantage: the upsell of small customers becomes more unrealistic)   The budget isn't by default 100k data points per month for each customer, it's based on the paid MAUs of the existing contracts e.g. 0.5 MAUs = 100k, 1.0 MAUs = 250k, 1.5 MAUs = 500k, 2 MAUs = 750k, .....
This ensures that there is budget for debugging and/or that every customer can export at least 1 experiment per month free of charge. If they become a regular user, they will need the upsell. The model would of course also be possible on an annual basis (#1).    Tool Solutions:   progress bar: The number of exported data points is displayed in the Bo, visible to every Kameleoon user (e.g. in the project section). Preferably with a progress bar and the applicable limit.  The popup also shows this view when the limit is exceeded. We build something like this hundreds of times as a shipping cost overview in experiments :)    user role: Only admin and/or production should be allowed to request raw data exports. If other roles try it, the popup should indicate that the correct role has been assigned. Alternatively individual users could also be assigned the "privilege" of raw data export regardless of their role, e.g. a data analyst only has marketing rights but is allowed to export   Tolerance limit: An export that only just exceeds the limit, e.g. 100,387 visits, will still be executed. However the user will receive a clear message that we have been generous and don't want to disrupt their work. It isn't possible to do this again. We are showing goodwill. The tolerance limit can remain secret.   History: similar to changes in experiments, there is an "export history" with date, time, Kameleoon user name and amount of data used. It creates maximum transparency in the team and may also help to better organize the team structure.

Title: SRM Redirects big problem consultant support
Details:
SRM and Redirects are are big problem for consultant & support.
It would be better to tell customer directly, while creating a redirect what they should do and what NOT:
https://help.kameleoon.com/url-redirection-split-test/
https://help.kameleoon.com/checking-for-potential-srm/#What_causes_SRM
Please check if we could get customers an advice to take care, if they don't follow this rules an SRM could appear!
help doc:
Check if the experiment is based on a redirection
This issue arises when some visitors redirected to variant B fail to see the page, or when data collection only occurs after page B loads. This results in data loss for variant B that wouldn’t happen on the original page.
⇒ To address this, we recommend:
Target only consented visitors using the following code in the targeting:
return Kameleoon.API.Visitor.experimentLegalConsent || false
Use the native redirection (under the variation options) OR Kameleoon.API.Core.processRedirect('newURL') instead of document.location.href = “newURL”
Don’t target the newURL where visitors are redirected, and ensure Kameleoon is installed on that newURL.
Implement a redirection on the original page as well, aligning its behavior with variant B. To set up the experiment effectively, you should have three variants:
Variant A: This variant should be disabled, with 0% traffic allocated to it.
Variant B: This serves as the new control variant, redirecting to itself (the page URL of the original version).
Variant C: This is the variant you want to test.

Title: Scheduled XML file import
Details:
Minimize errors in the product recommendations feed.

---

We currently risk having faulty data because there can be a big delay from feed generation to feed load. If we know when the feed is loaded, we can create the feed right before

---

Setting a specific time for importing XML files on an e-commerce website's recommendations block is crucial for ensuring the accuracy and timeliness of product recommendations. Here's why:
Freshness of Data: By setting a specific time for importing XML files, the system ensures that the latest updates from suppliers or product databases are included in the recommendations. This freshness of data is essential for providing customers with up-to-date information about products available for purchase.
Relevance to Customers: Customers expect relevant recommendations based on their current interests and preferences. Importing XML files at specific times allows the system to incorporate the most recent data, thereby increasing the relevance of product recommendations. This relevance enhances the overall user experience and increases the likelihood of conversion.
Competitive Advantage: In the highly competitive e-commerce landscape, staying ahead with the latest products and offerings is crucial. By importing XML files at specific times, the e-commerce website can ensure that its recommendations feature showcases the newest products, giving it a competitive edge over other platforms that may not update their recommendations as frequently.
Accurate Inventory Management: Setting a specific time for importing XML files also aids in accurate inventory management. By regularly updating product information, including availability and pricing, the system can prevent recommending out-of-stock items or displaying outdated prices, which can lead to customer frustration and loss of sales.
Optimized Performance: Importing XML files at specific times allows for better resource allocation and system performance optimization. By scheduling imports during off-peak hours or times of low website traffic, the system can minimize disruption to the user experience while ensuring that recommendations are continuously updated and available when customers visit the website.
In conclusion, setting a specific time for importing XML files is essential for maintaining the freshness, relevance, and accuracy of product recommendations on an e-commerce website. By prioritizing timely updates, the platform can provide customers with a superior shopping experience, gain a competitive advantage, and drive increased sales and customer satisfaction.

Title: Traffic expose feature for Web Experimentation
Details: In our Feature Flag experiments, we have the "expose traffic" option, which efficiently divides traffic within a single segment by prioritizing a larger share of users for critical tests. While working with the Leroy Merlin team, we encountered multiple front/backend projects requiring:   Mutually exclusive test setups (to avoid overlap),   Allocation of uneven traffic shares (for targeted distribution).   The absence of these features in Web Experimentation has imposed significant constraints, leading to:   Unnecessarily prolonged testing durations for key experiments.   Inability to prioritize projects with higher CPO values, undermining efficiency.   Ultimately, these limitations may lead clients to launch fewer projects. These two pain points are particularly critical for large-scale clients, as they directly impact scalability and strategic prioritization.

Title: Useful method fetches latest version widget code
Details:
It would be useful to have a method that fetches the latest version of a widget's code.
Currently, when we want to use a widget in the code editor, we face a major issue: if the widget is updated, the code editor doesn't reflect the latest version. This forces us to manually copy and paste the new code, and then modify it again — especially since all the element IDs change with each copy.
The idea is to have a function like dynamicInit(widgetId) that would dynamically apply the current version of the widget's code, as if it had been copy-pasted manually. This function would return the new widget ID, allowing us to store it in a variable and avoid any future code changes when the widget is updated.

Allow collective actions in the widget editor
Summary
Allow users to apply a same action to several elements or edit several elements at the same time.
User Story
As a user, I want to be able to select several elements of a widget and perform an action (for instance: delete, hide...) or edit the same property (for instance: position, size, alignment...) on all of them. This will be time saving.
Use Case
Users will use this feature to select several elements of a widget. They will be able to apply any action from a given list to all the elements selected.
They will also be able to edit some properties that all selected elements have. For example, they will be able to resize or change the position of all selected elements. If users select several text elements, they will be able to edit the font-size of all texts.
Requirements
- Users should be able to select several elements.
- Users should be able to select an action to apply to all elements at the same time.
- Actions should apply to all elements when users validate
- Users should be able to edit properties that all elements have
- Users should be able to edit properties that all selected elements share
- Changes should apply to all element when users validate

Title: check barrier free access
Details: Pain Point:   From mid-2025, websites and apps will be legally required to be barrier-free. This is regulated by the Barrier-Free Accessibility Strengthening Act (BFSG). The Barrierefreiheitsstärkungsgesetz (BFSG) implements the EU directive of the European Accessibility Act (EAA) so that standardised rules on accessibility apply throughout Europe. The regulations are based on the European standard EN 301 549, which in turn is largely based on the international guidelines for accessible web content (WCAG). e.g. sufficient contrast between foreground and background colour, links and buttons operable via the keyboard, screen reader compatibility of a website, etc.   Even if the website offers this accessibility on its live site, there is still a risk that the variant of an experiment or personalisation will not fulfil it. Such a design can have legal consequences and penalties.    Solution:   There are various features in Kameleoon that check for accessibility when changes are made. The contrast check of colours in new editors is a first step and a good example of this.

Title: synthetic method
Details:
I have one interesting question ’ve been asked on the pre-sale, about “synthetic” control method:
A synthetic control in the context of A/B testing on the web is a method of analysis that is used to create an artificial control group when a real control group cannot be obtained due to limitations in the experiment. Typically, a synthetic control is used when it is difficult or impossible to conduct a full randomized experiment with a real control group. Instead of relying solely on a real control group, it is possible to create a synthetic control group. This typically uses a statistical method that combines data from other groups, segments, or time to “simulate” the behavior that the control group might have if it existed.  It is easy to sell to a team launching the projects with 100% on Variation. For example: some marketing activities where test is going to diverted and client can not sacrifice traffic for AB tests and still wants so see what additional income they had.

Title: Добавление функционала в фильтр на странице результатов
Details:
Добавление функционала в фильтр на странице результатов.
Предлагаем добавить на странице результата в фильтрах выбор операции OR/AND, когда фильтр настраивается сразу по нескольким custom data или нескольким conversions. На данный момент при выборе несколько параметров, например elementName = “запись” и elementName = “узнать информацию” автоматически считаются только визиты, у которых есть оба значения за один визит, а хотелось бы иметь возможность посмотреть elementName = “запись” OR elementName = “узнать информацию”, чтобы посмотреть визиты, в которых пользователи кликали на кнопки только с elementName = “запись” или только с elementName = “узнать информацию” или elementName = “запись” и elementName = “узнать информацию”. Такая опция может быть полезна для сбора аналитики по нескольким объектам или по группе действий.
Второе улучшение, которое хотелось бы предложить: добавить в фильтры при выборе custom data возможность не просто полностью указать текст значения, но и указать часть текста, чтобы фильтровалось сразу по нескольким значениям custom data с операцией OR. Например, в custom data TextButton лежат значения: «Кухня на заказ», «Готовая кухня», «Дизайнерская кухня», «Записаться», при выборе фильтра по custom data, указав содержание строки «кухня», мы бы получили визиты, в рамках которых пользователь кликал по кнопкам «Кухня на заказ» или/и «Готовая кухня» или/и «Дизайнерская кухня». Такая опция могла бы помочь собрать общую аналитики по группе кнопок, при этом не лишая возможности рассмотреть детальнее клики по всем кнопкам страницы.
